title: Thunder Bluff
body: Thunder Bluff is the capital of the tauren, raised by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof on towering mesas at the northern end of Mulgore. For generations the tauren wandered as nomads, harried by the centaur, until Thrall and his orcs helped them win the plains, and Cairne built here a refuge where tauren of every tribe would be welcome. Great lifts, unique to the tauren, carry travelers up from the grass, while wind riders come and go above. Long bridges of wood and rope join the central mesa, where Cairne keeps his tent among the traders and craftsmen, to three outer rises: Elder Rise of the druids and elders, Spirit Rise of the shamans, with the Forsaken quarter hidden beneath it in the Pools of Vision, and Hunter Rise of the hunters and warriors. The peace on the bluff is real, but not untroubled. The Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem believes the tribes should be hers to lead, and some tauren wonder whether the pact with the Forsaken was made in haste.

title: The Central Mesa
body: The central mesa is the largest of Thunder Bluff's heights, climbing in tiers known as the lower, middle and high rises. Its tents hold the city's trade: the bank and the auction house, the inn where Innkeeper Pala greets every traveler like the wind on the plains, the forges of the Stonehoof smiths, the Winterhoof herbalists and alchemists, and the Mistrunner fishers and cooks. A great totem pole holds the wind rider roost, where Tal tends the beasts. Eyahn Eagletalon stitches a feathered headdress for a brother who will soon stand before the high chieftain. On the eastern heights rises the great tent of Cairne Bloodhoof, ringed by his Honor Guard.

title: Elder Rise
body: Elder Rise, east of the central mesa, is the seat of the elders and the druids of Thunder Bluff. Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem keeps his lodge here, and writings beside it set down the oldest legends of the Shu'halo: how the Earthmother breathed the plains into being, how in her grief she tore out her eyes to become An'she the sun and Mu'sha the moon, how Cenarius taught the first tauren to speak with the trees, and how the centaur fell upon the tribes once that teaching was forgotten. Piles of soil from Un'Goro rise beside the tents. Between the bridges stands the dwelling of Magatha Grimtotem, guarded by braves of her own tribe.

title: Spirit Rise
body: Spirit Rise, northwest of the central mesa, is the heart of shamanic learning in Thunder Bluff, and the Skychaser tribe holds great sway here. Skychaser trainers teach young shamans to hear the spirits, sending them out to answer the call of fire, while Xanis Flameweaver guides those ready to seek the spirits of water and air. The rise hides more than it shows. Just below its cap, reached by a path that is easy to miss near the bridge, opens a warren of caves called the Pools of Vision, where the Forsaken keep their quarter.

title: The Pools of Vision
body: Beneath Spirit Rise lie the Pools of Vision, a warren of caves that serves as the Forsaken quarter of Thunder Bluff. Mages and priests of the Undercity teach here, and mages who return to the bluff by spell arrive among the pools. Apothecary Zamah speaks for the Royal Apothecary Society, the emissary of the Forsaken to their tauren allies, and the widow Clarice Foster nurses a grievance of her own. The path down to it from the rise is well hidden.

title: Hunter Rise
body: Hunter Rise, south of the central mesa, is the home of Thunder Bluff's hunters and warriors. In Hunter's Hall the Thunderhorns teach the bow and the bond between hunter and beast, Hesuwa Thunderhorn trains companions, and the Ragetotems drill young warriors. Melor Stonehoof sends seasoned hunters after quarry across the world. Mosarn's forge turns out arms and armor in great volume to outfit the braves who defend tauren lands. Battlemasters of the Horde call fighters from the rise to Warsong Gulch, Arathi Basin and Alterac Valley.

title: Cairne Bloodhoof
body: Cairne Bloodhoof, high chieftain of the tauren, was old when the Third War began, chief of the Bloodhoof tribe while the centaur hunted his people. He watched the young Warchief Thrall cut down centaur raiders and pledged the tauren to the Horde, and the orcs helped him win Mulgore in return. Here he raised Thunder Bluff, a refuge from the burdens of the world, and drew the scattered tribes together, and he stood behind the pact that brought the Forsaken into the Horde. He keeps his rival Magatha close, on Elder Rise, and still asks young tauren who reach his door to prove themselves in the hunt, beginning with the horn of the great kodo Arra'chea.

title: Magatha Grimtotem
body: Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone, is matriarch of the Grimtotem tribe and a powerful shaman. She became its matriarch through an arranged marriage and took the lead when her mate died in an unforeseen climbing accident, and she holds that she alone is fit to rule the tauren. Cairne lets her dwell on Elder Rise, keeping his rival close. She is the Forsaken's warmest friend, hoping tauren ways can help them become human again, and she buys Highborne tablets from Azshara through the orc Jediga. Far from the bluff, in Stonetalon, Thousand Needles and Feralas, Grimtotem braves attack every outsider.

title: Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem
body: Hamuul Runetotem, childhood friend of Cairne Bloodhoof, was moved by the druids who stood at Mount Hyjal, and afterward sought out Malfurion Stormrage to learn their ways. He became the first tauren druid in nearly twenty generations and now leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle on Elder Rise. He helped persuade Thrall to accept the Forsaken into the Horde. The earth keeps many secrets, he teaches, and some must stay secret for the good of all. He has walked the Emerald Dream seeking the taint in the Barrens, and he urges those he sends to Moonglade to look past the growing tension between Darnassus and the Circle.

title: Nara Wildmane
body: Nara Wildmane is a young druid of Elder Rise with a fierce spirit. When Hamuul Runetotem entered the land of dreams in search of the taint creeping through the Barrens, the old druid could not stay long, but Nara remained in the dreaming after he fled, and what she saw there haunts her still. Her travels have taken her as far as the Valley of the Watchers in the Tanaris desert. Those who find strange magic among the wildkin are sent to her, for she is an expert in that lore, and she counts among her friends the druid Mulgris Deepriver, who went alone to the Plaguelands to tend its suffering creatures.

title: Apothecary Zamah
body: Apothecary Zamah is a scholar of the Royal Apothecary Society and the Forsaken's emissary to the tauren, working from the Pools of Vision. Her heart no longer beats, she says, yet she still grieves for the wounded spirits of Stonetalon. She serves the Dark Lady openly. She studies serpentbloom, a rare herb from the darkest depths of the Wailing Caverns that she believes holds great potential, though many she sent for it never came back, and she takes in the rendered spores her colleague Helbrim gathers in the Barrens. When the tauren ask the Forsaken for help, Zamah gives it gladly.

Once her toxin has been planted among the goblins of Stonetalon, she tells the one who carried it to put aside any guilt, for the Venture Company has earned much worse. And if the Forsaken can teach their allies a single wisdom, she adds, it is that a dark road is worth taking when it ends in victory.

title: Sage Truthseeker
body: Sage Truthseeker is one of the sages of Thunder Bluff, historians whose learning is known throughout the Horde, and he keeps his tent on the central mesa. Visitors who march into his tent with purpose in their stride are asked whether they seek his counsel, or a mystery of the universe revealed. He is loyal to Cairne and would trust the chieftain with his life. It is the others around him that he does not trust, least of all the Forsaken, whose history he finds thick with deceit.

title: Melor Stonehoof
body: Melor Stonehoof is a master hunter of Hunter Rise, and older hunters send him the most promising of the young. Old Skorn Whitecloud of Bloodhoof Village tests them first with the claws of Mulgore's flatland prowlers; Melor then sends them on to the Barrens, whose strong-willed beasts teach a young hunter's spirit to grow. Tauren hunt, he teaches, at times for food, at times for honor and at times to earn the Earthmother's teachings, and every hunt carries its own lesson. When his students have grown, he sends word for them to return, for there are harder hunts still.

title: Tahu Sagewind and Aponi Brightmane
body: Near the druids' lodge on Elder Rise, two young tauren pass the days in talk. Aponi Brightmane, a warrior, was sent home from the war in Northrend with an infected wound in her arm, and she chafes at sitting idle while her band fights on. Tahu Sagewind, a student of Hamuul Runetotem, tends her. He has heard the elves of Moonglade speak of their moon goddess, and he muses that what Hamuul teaches is the lore of the night elves. The Shu'halo strive for balance in all things, and he wonders whether the druids have overlooked some part of it. Aponi answers with hope: the dawn will come, and even on the glacier the sun breaks through the gloom.

title: Auld Stonespire
body: Auld Stonespire honors Cairne Bloodhoof for uniting the tauren on the bluff, but he cannot forgive the past as easily as some. For decades his people lived in the southern Barrens, on land they held holy, until enemy after enemy drove them out. Chief among them, in his eyes, are the quilboar of Razorfen Kraul, where the crone Charlga Razorflank now musters a foul army. To drive a people from holy land, he says, is a sin that earns the most severe revenge, and only when Razorflank's heart is brought to him will he be able to die in peace.
sources: quest 1102 description, request and reward
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: his grievance and his wish for Razorflank's heart are the premise of 1102, which stays with the Barrens. Earlier: Razorfen Kraul and quest 1102 belong to the Barrens; only the TALK trigger is used. No gossip menu, quest dialog via 1102. Faction 2: template 104. Verified.

title: Forsaken Aid
body: The spirits of Stonetalon cry out as the Venture Company strips the mountains of their forests, and the Horde shaman Seereth Stonebreak, unable to calm them alone, has sought counsel from the one tauren elder she knows by name: Magatha Grimtotem. The Elder Crone's answer is unexpected. To heal the land, she says, its disease must first be removed, and the Forsaken know disease better than anyone; asking their help will also strengthen the trust between the two peoples. Her servant carries word of Stonetalon ahead to Apothecary Zamah in the Pools of Vision, a scholar and emissary of the Forsaken, and the one who brought the plea is sent after it.
sources: quests 1061 to 1063 (Stonetalon start, Seereth, The Elder Crone)
quest 1064 description
creature_text 4046 (Magatha sends a messenger to Zamah)
quests 1065, 1066, 1067, 1086 descriptions and reward texts
quest 1063 (ended by Magatha)
notes: Converted: Zamah's answer moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 1064), Lydon's toxin plan to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 1065, which offers 1066), the finished toxin to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 1067), the fogger, the sky port and Zamah's verdict to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 1086). DONE 1066 is Hillsbrad's (Lydon 26715 part 3) and is not used; the blood's gathering is only implied by part 3. The Stonetalon lead in (1061 to 1063) is only summed up. Faction 2: AllowableRaces 690 (1065 is 0, but Zamah and Lydon are Horde only). Earlier: Triggered on 1064, the first quest sorted to Thunder Bluff; the Stonetalon lead in (1061 from Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar, 1062, 1063) is left to Stonetalon. Hillsbrad's Apothecary Lydon entry only mentions the toxin; its quests (1065 to 1067) are not used there. Faction 2: AllowableRaces 690. Verified. Check: part 1 reworded so it does not repeat Zamah's opening; part 3 (ACCEPT 1067) tells only what 1067's own text says (the toxin is ready, take it to Zamah), nothing of Hillsbrad's Lydon part 3 (DONE 1066).

parts.body: Zamah has been told to expect the visit. Dead though she is, she still feels sorrow for Stonetalon's spirits, and the Forsaken are eager to help. The goblins must be dealt with by extreme measures, extreme but without bloodshed, and her colleague Lydon in Tarren Mill, far off in the Hillsbrad Foothills of Lordaeron, may have just the tool. A note detailing her needs goes to him.
sources: quest 1064 reward text
quest 1065 description

parts.body: Lydon knows at once what to do. He will brew a toxin to bleed the violence from the Venture Company and leave the goblins weak and docile. It needs the blood of innocents, a hard thing to come by, but the Syndicate shadow mages of Durnholde Keep collect such blood for unsavory purposes of their own.
sources: quest 1065 reward text
quest 1066 description (offered by Lydon on turning in 1065)

parts.body: The toxin is made, and Lydon, thrilled to see his work applied in the field, promises favorable, perhaps even contagious, results. Before it is used, though, it must go back across the sea to Zamah, who will devise a way to deliver it.
sources: quest 1067 description

parts.body: Zamah fits the toxin into a fogger, and it is carried to Stonetalon and planted at the Venture Company's small sky port, where flying machines ferry messages and light cargo, in the hope that it finds its way to the company's headquarters. Feel no guilt, Zamah says afterward; the goblins deserve far worse. Never shy from dark paths, if they lead to victory.
sources: quest 1067 reward text
quest 1086 description and reward text
item 5638 Toxic Fogger
creature_text 3419

title: Magatha's Lost Clansman
body: Troggs have begun to climb out of the lava filled depths beneath Orgrimmar into Ragefire Chasm. Magatha Grimtotem, it is said, sought to make peace with them, but they turned on her diplomats and killed them, and now she names them a threat to the whole Horde. Her servant Rahauro sends heroes into the Chasm to thin the troggs before they can overwhelm the orcs from below. The troggs were not all that drew the Elder Crone's eye. One of her clansmen, Maur Grimtotem, found something peculiar in the Chasm and never came out to show her. She wants his body found, if anything is left of it, and any sign of what he discovered.
sources: quest 5723 description and reward
quest 5722 description and reward
quest 5724 description, request and reward
npc_text 4473 (Rahauro gossip)
notes: Converted: the troggs thinned moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 5723), the body and the satchel to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 5722, QUEST_ACCEPT 5724, both at Maur's body), the satchel handed over to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 5724). 5723 and 5722 run side by side, so parts 1 and 2 each read on from the opening alone. The satchel's contents are never stated. Earlier: Both quests start from Rahauro 11833 on Elder Rise; no prerequisites. Orgrimmar's Hidden Enemies covers the Searing Blade in Ragefire Chasm, not this. The satchel's contents are never stated, so nothing is claimed. Faction 2: AllowableRaces 690. Verified.

parts.body: With the troggs' numbers cut down, Rahauro is glad the task was taken seriously, for the creatures will find it harder to reach the surface now. Yet he muses that one day someone should learn where such creatures come from, and what they truly want.
sources: quest 5723 reward text

parts.body: Maur's body lies in the dark of the Chasm, battered by clubs and fists, his clothing and gear still upon him, for the troggs care little for wealth. Beneath him is a satchel, still gripped tight in his arms, as though he died trying to protect it.
sources: quest 5722 reward text (ended at Maur Grimtotem 11834)
quest 5724 description (started by 11834)

parts.body: Rahauro had hoped for some clue to why one of Magatha's clan had to die so needlessly. He takes the satchel for his mistress without a word of what it holds, and hands over the reward she left for whoever found her clansman.
sources: quest 5724 request and reward texts

title: Portents of Uldum
body: Since miniature discs were carried out of Uldaman, the sages of Thunder Bluff, historians known throughout the Horde, have had much to discuss. Sage Truthseeker has turned all his energies to them, and in talking the find over with the druid Nara Wildmane on Elder Rise he came upon an unexpected thread: her past travels to the Valley of the Watchers in the Tanaris desert, which may hold the next step. He means to send whoever brought him the discs to hear what she remembers.
sources: quest 2278 and 2280 descriptions (miniature discs, sages of Thunder Bluff)
quest 2440 description
quest 2965 description and reward
quests 2966, 2954, 2967 descriptions and rewards
quest 2968 description and reward
notes: Converted: Uldum named and the discs sent south moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2965), the stone watcher and the missing plates to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2966 and 2954, both at the pedestal), Nara's fears and the impasse to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 2967). Ironforge's Secrets of the Creators uses 2279, 2946, 2964 (the Alliance road), none of these. Earlier: Reframed around Truthseeker and Nara so it does not retell Ironforge's Secrets of the Creators; Uldaman disc mechanics and the watcher's speech cut back. Check: opening reworded so it does not repeat Sage Truthseeker's part 1 (DONE 2280).

parts.body: The translated glyphs of the discs name Uldum, a place most think a myth. Nara knows better, for she has stood outside its sealed gates in the Valley of the Watchers. The sage and the druid send the discs south to those gates, unsure whether anything at all will happen, or what.
sources: quest 2965 reward text
quest 2966 description

parts.body: Something does. Before the gates of Uldum the discs hum and glow, and a stone watcher springs to life, a guardian of entry. The discs alone are not enough, it says: the missing Plates of Uldum must be joined to them before anyone may enter.
sources: quest 2966 reward text (ended at the pedestal 142343)
quest 2954 description and reward text

parts.body: Back on Elder Rise, Nara likens the discs to keys on a ring, of which the plates are the missing ones. She does not know whether to be excited or terrified, and fears that secrets of the earth which could destroy everyone may lie within. For now the sages wait, sifting their lore for where the plates might lie, and hope soon to call their helper back.
sources: quest 2967 reward text
quest 2968 description (offered by Nara on turning in 2967)

title: Morrowgrain Research
body: Innkeepers across the Horde pass on a request: Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem needs seasoned helpers for a dangerous research project of the Cenarion Circle. The soil of Un'Goro Crater is said to be rich with potent magic, and the Circle wants it in great quantity. It lies in piles across the crater, and some of the beasts there carry it on them. Once gathered it is unloaded onto piles on Elder Rise under the eye of Ghede, a druid who barks at every helper like a drill sergeant at a raw recruit and has no patience for anything cute or funny.
sources: quests 3762, 936, 3784 descriptions (Pala, Gryshka, Norman)
quest 3761 description, request and reward
npc_text 2333 (Ghede gossip)
quest 3782 description and reward (Evergreen Pouch, Tharlendris seeds, my daughter Bashana, cost)
quests 3786 and 3804 texts (night elves conducting similar research)
notes: Converted: the purpose of the soil (the pouch, the seeds, morrowgrain, Bashana) moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 3782, offered by Hamuul after 3761); the night elves' parallel research and the open mystery to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 3804, Bashana's repeatable turn-in). Opening filled out from 3761 (soil in piles and on beasts). Earlier: Entry points: 3762 (Innkeeper Pala 6746), 936 (Innkeeper Gryshka 6929, Orgrimmar), 3784 (Innkeeper Norman 6741, Undercity), all leading to 3761, which Hamuul also offers directly. Orgrimmar and Undercity entries do not use these. Faction 2: AllowableRaces 690. Verified.

parts.body: The soil is wanted for a purpose. In an evergreen pouch it nourishes Tharlendris seeds, which blossom into an array of potent herbs, and one of them, morrowgrain, is a mystery the Arch Druid hopes to unravel for the Circle. His daughter Bashana hands out the costly seeds, and those who run out must buy more from her.
sources: quest 3782 description and reward text

parts.body: Bashana gathers the morrowgrain ten at a time for her father. The night elves, she says, are studying the same herbs, to what end no one knows, and the Arch Druid believes the need for morrowgrain will last until the secret of the herb is found.
sources: quest 3804 completion and reward text (auto-complete, so QUEST_DONE)

title: The Hunter's Path
body: Once tales of a young champion's deeds reach him, Melor Stonehoof sends word, and the hunts he sets after that are of another kind. At times, he teaches, the tauren hunt for food, at times for honor and at times to earn the Earthmother's teachings, but this hunt is none of those. The hyena Steelsnap is a tyrant of the Thousand Needles, living outside the Earthmother's blessing, drawing other hyenas to him and spreading fear and bloodshed among gentler beasts. Another hunt is a mercy. Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk of Dustwallow Marsh, still moves with the speed of youth, but his aging body tortures the great spirit within it, and the hunter's task is to lead him to peace.
sources: quest 1130 description
quest 1131 description and reward
quest 1136 description and reward
quest 1205 description and reward
notes: Converted: Steelsnap's death and the call to Alterac moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 1131), Frostmaw's defeat and Melor's verdict to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 1136), Deadmire's end to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 1205, which has no prerequisite, so part 3 reads on from the opening alone). 1130 stays with the Barrens. Earlier: Opening no longer says the quests are for hunters (no class limit in the DB); Deadmire called another hunt, since 1205 has no prerequisite.

parts.body: Steelsnap falls, and with him a horrible taint is cleansed from the Thousand Needles. That is the lesson of the day, Melor says, and he judges the hunter ready for far-off lands: the white yeti Frostmaw of the Alterac Mountains, so elusive in the snows that Melor writes out on a scroll how he may be lured.
sources: quest 1131 reward text
quest 1136 description (offered after 1131)

parts.body: Frostmaw's mane is brought back to Hunter Rise. Both strength and cunning were needed to find and defeat the yeti, Melor declares, and the hunter has both. The path has led from the valleys of the Needles to the heights of Alterac, and in time, such being the way of the hunter, it will lead through all the Earthmother's lands.
sources: quest 1136 reward text

parts.body: The tooth of Deadmire is brought back from the marsh, and the old crocolisk's long, maddening pain is ended. The hunt was surely not easy, Melor allows, but it is good to know the beast's suffering is over at last.
sources: quest 1205 description, request and reward texts

title: Too Hasty a Pact
body: The tauren helped open the way for the Forsaken into the Horde, and not every voice on the bluff approves. Some feel pity: the alchemist Bena Winterhoof wept when she first saw the undead, and then the Earthmother sang in her blood and told her to save them. Magatha Grimtotem is among the elders who champion them. Sage Truthseeker is not persuaded. The Earthen Ring meant only good toward the plagued, he grants, but who knows what voices whisper in the ears of the Elder Council? The Forsaken have a history thick with deceit, the pact was made too hastily, and Cairne might have done better to heed the warnings from Orgrimmar. Before advising his chieftain, he wants the Compendium of the Fallen, kept by crazed human zealots in the Scarlet Monastery, whose mad research may yet prove useful.
sources: quest 1049 description, request and reward
npc_text 5079 (Bena Winterhoof gossip)
quest 3518 description (Magatha proponent of the alliance)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Hamuul_Runetotem and Cairne_Bloodhoof (tauren role in bringing the Forsaken into the Horde)
notes: Converted: the Compendium's recovery moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 1049); the opening tightened to the Story range. npc_text 5079 (Bena) reread: era-neutral. 1049 excludes the Forsaken (AllowableRaces 674). Earlier: Magatha 'in council' made general (3518: among the elders, a proponent of the alliance).

parts.body: The Compendium of the Fallen comes back from the Scarlet Monastery, and Truthseeker, who had begun to wonder whether the book existed at all, rejoices. It is only one piece of a complicated puzzle, yet the one who brought it has served the tauren of Thunder Bluff well, and that dedication, he promises, will not be forgotten.
sources: quest 1049 request and reward texts
